title: Cohesion and coupling
idea: Cohesion is how closely a class's parts serve one purpose; coupling is how much one class depends on another's details. Aim for high cohesion, low coupling.
points: A cohesive class has methods that mostly use the same fields.
Coupling grows with every class you import, construct or reach into.
Depend on a small method shape, and inject the object that provides it.
Count the files one change touches; many files means the design leaks.

code.title: Cohesive, loosely coupled
code.caption: Swap `fakePayments` for any object with a `charge` method. `Checkout` does not change.

walk.text: `Cart` owns its items, and both methods use `#items`: high cohesion.
A fake gateway is enough to run it; no payment library is imported.
Build the parts at the edge, then connect them.

code.title: Ask, do not dig
code.caption: Both print the same today. Rename `address` and you fix one method in `Order`, not every caller like `tightLabel`.

pitfalls: Do not split a class until its methods stop sharing fields.
Avoid calling `new` on concrete helpers inside business logic; inject them.
Replace long chains like `order.customer.address.city` with a method on the owner.

quiz.q: `ReportService` imports nine classes, and each method uses different fields. What is true?
quiz.why: Methods sharing no fields means the class does several jobs. Nine imports means many classes can break it.

takeaway: Keep related things together and talk to others through small interfaces.

starters: How do I tell if a class has low cohesion?
